messages:
customer_io: Hey team — our mobile app hit repeated streaming drops during a 90s generation. Client received partial final tokens then entered a reconnect loop. Approx time 2025-11-28T10:16:40Z. Uploaded short pcap and raw client logs to the support ticket.

anya: Sorry about that — can you paste the minimal repro curl / SDK call and any trace IDs? Also was the client using HTTP/1.1 or HTTP/2? :eyes:

customer_io: Repro steps:
1) iOS app opens SSE to /v1/stream
2) Sends prompt, gets several chunks then a short gap, connection drops with ECONNRESET and an immediate reconnect storm.
Curl used to repro locally:
```
curl -N -H "Accept: text/event-stream" \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "X-RW-Trace: 1738204567" \
  -d '{"model":"gpt-neo-2","input":"long prompt ...","stream":true}' \
  https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream
```
Trace header: 1738204567
PCAP: s3://redwood-support-temp/pcaps/1738204567.pcap

sam: Quick checks while we triage:
- Any 502/504 from edge before/after the reset?
- Token rotate during session? Mid-session auth swaps can trigger retries that close sockets.

customer_io: No 502 in client logs. No token rotation. I can repro with curl (HTTP/1.1). Forcing --http2 avoids the disconnect but increases chunk latency.

marc: I pulled the pcap. RST/FIN originates from edge (198.51.100.23), not backend. Hypotheses: edge keepalive timeout or proxy buffering+flush. Will check edge logs for upstream close or `client closed connection` messages.

li-chen: Repro checklist:
- tcpdump on client during curl:
```
sudo tcpdump -i any -s0 -w streaming-1738204567.pcap 'tcp port 443 and host 198.51.100.23'
```
- Try `curl --no-buffer --http1.1`
- Toggle heartbeat header `X-RW-Heartbeat: 15` to keep socket active for long generations.

anya: Also enable debug headers so we can correlate: set `X-RW-Debug: 1` + trace id. We'll pull server logs for trace=1738204567. We have the S3 pcap path and will download it.

ops-bot: New artifact uploaded: s3://redwood-support-temp/pcaps/1738204567.pcap (3.2MB)

marc: From pcap: backend delivers final chunk, ~120ms later edge sends TCP RST to client. Backend's connection still alive. That points to edge-level idle or router reparenting.

li-chen: Check proxy config: `proxy_buffering` and `proxy_read_timeout` on the SSE route. If proxy buffers until a threshold, chunk semantics look wrong and can cause abrupt closes.

sam: Mitigations for customer while we investigate: increase heartbeat to 10s, set client reconnect jittered exponential backoff, try forcing HTTP/2 if that avoids RST.

customer_io: Will try heartbeat 10s and report. One more thing — can you confirm billing/auth impact? We want to avoid double-charges from reconnects.

anya: We checked request logs for trace=1738204567 — only one billed request id recorded. Short reconnects are deduped in billing; we'll confirm with billing and update the ticket.

marc: Eng-sre action items:
- Inspect edge logs for trace=1738204567 for close reason and upstream timeouts
- Confirm `proxy_read_timeout` and keepalive settings on the route
- Reproduce in lab with proxy buffering toggled and capture pcaps

li-chen: Fast repro tip: deploy a minimal nginx reverse proxy with default `proxy_buffering on` in front of an SSE server and run the curl; default nginx keepalive settings often surface this.

anya: Customer — thanks for the repro. Please run `--no-buffer` + heartbeat 10s test and upload new pcap if you still see RST. We'll escalate to infra if edge logs show premature termination. :thumbsup:

customer_io: Thanks all — running tests now, will upload new pcap once done.
